primitives.name: Tidal Capital Accumulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is like the oft-cited advance of the tide up a beach, advance and recession alternating and obscuring even the fact that a small gain of an occasional wave constitutes a net advance.
primitives.assumptions: Capital growth occurs in discrete pulses modulated by cyclical trends; net gain emerges from stochastic fluctuations over time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When wave amplitude exceeds critical threshold, leading to irreversible loss of capital stock.

layer2.mapping: The tidal metaphor mirrors GSI's probabilistic capital evolution model, where each wave represents a stochastic increment in capital formation under bounded uncertainty.
layer2.telemetry: Aggregate capital stock variance over time periods

primitives.name: Credit Expansion Instability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Price levels and profit margins being even more dependent on this precarious exchange medium, the operations of business proper find themselves tied up to the tendencies of a credit currency under private control to expand to a point of instability and under the least shock to collapse.
primitives.assumptions: Business operations depend on credit availability; instability arises when credit expands beyond sustainable thresholds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collapse occurs when σ > 1, indicating exponential divergence in monetary expansion.

layer2.mapping: GSE models credit-driven instability using feedback loops in P(t) and C(t), where instability manifests as a phase transition in market equilibrium states.
layer2.telemetry: Volatility of price-to-capital ratio during credit booms

primitives.name: Capital-Forming Cycles
primitives.verbatim_quote: Economic progress under real conditions shows similar advance and recession, proceeding in cycles of a character now fairly well understood, but of such uncertain length that the consequences at the turningpoints are often catastrophic.
primitives.assumptions: Economic activity follows periodic oscillations with unknown duration; turning points cause abrupt shifts in growth trajectory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At T_cycle → ∞, system loses coherence and enters chaotic regime.

layer2.mapping: GSI employs cyclic autoregressive models to predict turning points in capital formation based on recurrence patterns observed in historical data.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency domain analysis of capital flow time series

This aligns with GSI’s Bayesian inference framework, wherein each wave contributes to a posterior belief about capital formation, modeled through recursive update rules. The instability induced by credit expansion (primitive 2) introduces a feedback mechanism that can destabilize the system, akin to a bifurcation in dynamical systems theory. In GSE, this translates into state transitions governed by credit dynamics, where collapse or growth depends on whether the system remains within stable attractors. The cyclical nature of capital formation (primitive 3) further reinforces these transitions, suggesting that economic regimes shift according to predictable yet unpredictable temporal patterns. These primitives form a triadic structure: stochastic input (waves), feedback control (credit), and temporal modulation (cycles). Their interplay defines both the structure of uncertainty and the pathways of systemic change.
